Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  Acute wheezing and shortness of breath for 2 days after heavy dust exposure while cleaning; worse at night; sometimes unable to complete sentences. History of childhood asthma with occasional exercise-induced symptoms. Seasonal hay fever. No chest pain with deep breaths. No dizziness. Hydrating adequately.
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Not recorded.
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Asthma inhaler on hand from a few months ago (type and dose/route/frequency not documented); not used for this episode. Prior courses of oral steroids for asthma (historical; current dose/route/frequency not documented). No antihistamines at home. No regular medications otherwise recorded. No known drug allergies reported.
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Not recorded.
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Smoking status not recorded. Alcohol and other substances not recorded. Physical activity: reports that prolonged running can trigger wheeze. Dust exposure during house cleaning immediately preceded current symptoms.
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Not recorded.
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  Able to access GP clinic within minutes’ drive. Privacy during call confirmed. Other social factors not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key clinical findings:  2-day history of worsening wheeze and dyspnea beginning ~1 hour after heavy dust exposure; nocturnal worsening; sometimes unable to complete sentences; history of childhood asthma and seasonal hay fever; no chest pain or dizziness; has not used inhaler; no objective vitals available via telehealth.
- Working diagnosis:  Acute asthma exacerbation triggered by dust/allergen exposure. Supported by atopic history (hay fever), prior asthma (including past steroid use), nocturnal worsening, wheeze after a clear environmental trigger, and severity limiting speech. Consistent with DDx (high likelihood).
- Considerations (from DDx, consistent with transcript):  
  - Irritant-induced bronchospasm from dust exposure (medium likelihood): fits temporal relationship to dust; absence of infectious symptoms.  
  - Allergic rhinitis with lower-airway involvement (medium likelihood): atopic background and dust trigger, though nasal symptoms not reported.
- Plan:  
  - Same-day in-person GP assessment arranged; clinician to send letter via app.  
  - At clinic: measure oxygen saturation (pulse oximetry) and assess need for additional testing/treatment.  
  - Trial of OTC antihistamine suggested en route or at clinic if obtainable.  
  - Possible need for steroids to be determined after in-person assessment.  
- Conflict noted:  This documentation template is for adults 55+, while the patient reports age 40.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute asthma exacerbation triggered by dust/allergen exposure — High likelihood: Atopy (hay fever), prior asthma (including past steroid use), nocturnal worsening, and onset after dust exposure with wheeze and dyspnea limiting speech.
- Irritant-induced bronchospasm from dust exposure — Medium likelihood: Temporal relationship to heavy dust without infectious prodrome.
- Allergic rhinitis with lower-airway involvement — Medium likelihood: Atopic background and dust trigger, though absence of nasal/ocular symptoms.

Quality checks

- Missing expected elements: No vitals (BP, pulse, SpO2), BMI/anthropometrics, smoking status, immunisation review (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus), chronic disease screening (lipids, glucose/HbA1c), urinalysis, and preventive cancer screening status not recorded. No objective respiratory measures (peak flow, auscultation).
- Internal conflicts/contradictions: Age 40 vs this being an Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 55+ template); conflict noted.
- Transcript quality notes: Partial loss of video; brief audio drop (“Such as check your …”); otherwise history obtained; no physical exam possible via telehealth.
